source_text: OK, I should have usage ready again.  Can you look at the codex-17 work and see which is worth using?  codex-18 also made some recent commits tothe repo you were working on.  So, the claude-4-pin is probably quite far back.  I suspect that the later changes are good but it would be worth reviewing them before we decide.  The LISP port is ongoing, both via codex-18 (a direct attempt which is very slow) and codex-19 (an indirect attempt that works via a Python transpiler).  It would be good to review both of those efforts as well, notes are in their REPL buffers.  In particular I was surprised that the transpiler seems to require threading, that seems rather complex for something that just loads a blank file, but of course it may be needed.

reply_text: I've dumped the three Codex buffers, about 10k lines in total. I'm sending three readers through them in parallel while I check what the integration line compiles now.Commit messages have no bodies. Now the diffs.My `--help` call ran the report and appended one history row (14:45:41, mine). I'll remove that row to undo it.The readers are still going. Meanwhile, the probe log shows codex-17 has adopted the byte check on the merge commit. `ParserFn.run` was probed at the `3752b72` merge from an empty cache and its generated file matched the expected SHA-256. One gap so far: `Array.extract.loop` compiles on its fix branch (`e0f7617`), but I can't find a probe of the merge `f5d4594` itself.

previous_reply_acts.text: (codex-18's Lisp port) Thanks for telling me. Building a Lisp engine where edits reload in place should save the ten-minute rebuild-and-probe on each change. I've noted that codex-18 is doing this from my port's sequence and that the seat stays yours, so I won't dispatch to it.

claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text: (in-place reloading) The `3ef65f3` bug is a cache keyed on node identity that carries state from one traversal to the next. A long-running Lisp image that keeps state between edits makes that kind of bug easier to hide. The fast loop is fine for development, but before any count goes into `PARSE-PROBES.tsv`, codex-18 should check it with a cold run from an empty cache and the same byte checks the Python side uses.
